chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) used to supplicate with this supplication during the Month of Ramadan:
O Allah! It is to You I beseech, and from You I seek my needs. (There are) ones who seek needs from people, but I do not seek my needs except from You alone, there being no associates for You;

and I ask You by Your grace and Your pleasure that You send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the People of his Household. And that You make for me in this year a way to Your Sacred House — a hajj pilgrimage that is righteous, accepted, pure, and devoted solely to You, by which my eyes are delighted and my rank is raised,

and grant me that I lower my gaze and guard my chastity and refrain by it from all of Your prohibitions until there is nothing more preferable to me than obedience to You, fearing You, acting according to what You love, and abandoning what You abhor and forbid.

And make all of that easy, prosperous, and with well-being, and inspire me with gratitude for what You have bestowed upon me. And I ask You to make my death a martyr's death in Your way, under the banner of Your Prophet, alongside Your friends. And I ask You to vanquish Your enemies and the enemies of Your Messenger through me.

And I ask You to honor me by humiliating whoever You wish from Your creatures, and do not humiliate me through honoring any of Your friends. O Allah! Make for me a way with the Messenger. Sufficient for me is Allah — whatever Allah wills.

key_terms.أَتَوَسَّلُ: Tawassul — seeking intercession or closeness to God through particular means
key_terms.أَوْزِعْنِي: Awzi'ni — inspire me, make me inclined to, instill in me
key_terms.رِضْوَانِكَ: Ridwan — divine pleasure, approval, contentment with the servant
key_terms.مَبْرُورَةً: Mabrur — a hajj accepted by God, characterized by righteousness and absence of sin
key_terms.مَحَارِمِكَ: Maharim — the divine prohibitions, things Allah has forbidden

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam Sadiq recite during Ramadan?
ai.summary: This is a comprehensive supplication narrated by Abu Baseer, who reported that Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) regularly recited it during the holy month of Ramadan. The supplication embodies exclusive reliance on God (tawakkul), contrasting the believer who turns only to Allah against those who seek needs from people. It encompasses requests for hajj, moral refinement (lowering the gaze, guarding chastity), martyrdom in God's cause, and victory over His enemies — reflecting the holistic spiritual and combative nature of Islamic piety during Ramadan.
